study_order: Study order. Chapters 1–2 set the ground rules: course logistics, the number-systems refresher every later chapter leans on, and the ethics and law that separate a security professional from a criminal. Chapter 3 is the conceptual core (CIA, threats and attacks, the first look at cryptography, passwords, and access control) and carries your professor's "worth notice" list, marked ★ in its exam checklist. Chapter 4 is the math-heavy one: block ciphers, modes, RSA, and hashing. Chapters 5–6 apply everything to operating systems, first UNIX and then Windows. The course is cumulative, so earlier chapters stay fair game on later exams. The formula sheet at the back collects every formula in one place.
tool_note: This section has an interactive calculator on the course website. Work the problems by hand first; exams are closed-tool.
